newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks lower after strong start.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks lower after strong start.

text.p: Shares on the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) closed slightly lower at the end of a week's trading on Friday despite promising prospects it showed at the start of the week, traders said.
The 41-share CSE index, set at 100 points, closed at 83.85 on Friday from 84.48 a week ago, losing 0.75 percent of its value.
The market had opened on a bull run on Monday with gains of 1.01 percent, closing at 85.33 points, the highest mark seen on the market this month. The gains were lost as the week progressed.
"We saw signs of a recovery last Friday and Monday," said Stavros Agrotis of CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation.
"We expected this pattern on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday... on Tuesday it was quiet which again means that investor confidence is not quite back yet."
Confidence took a blow when investors realised foreigners would not be queuing up after the launch of the official exchange on March 29, he said.

"The market was expensive and too small to draw the attention of bigger operations abroad," said Agrotis. "The messages investors were getting through the media all this time were also negative," he said.

The launch of the official stockmarket coincided with renewed tension on the island. Turkey has occupied a third of Cyprus since 1974, when it invaded after a short-lived coup backed by the military then ruling Greece.
Economic growth in 1996 also registered a slowdown to 2.5 percent of GDP from five percent recorded in 1995, mainly due to a decline in tourist arrivals by four percent to an estimated two million.
Agrotis said he expected the market to pick up again before the end of the month, the deadline for the release of half-yearly results by companies on the exchange.
"When we see positive results in a certain sector we will see some action," he said. "As soon as the investors make a profit there they will move onto something else."
All seven sub indices were steady on last week's figures. Banking stocks closed at 91.12, from 91.61 last week.

Fully-paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed at 346, shedding 2.5 cents from last week's close of 348.5. Fully-paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank went down one cent to close at 323.5. Fully paid shares of Hellenic Bank lost gains made during the week to close at 258.5, still two cents higher than last week.
The sub index for tourism enterprises closed higher at 74.79 from 73.41 last week, while the index of the insurance sector closed at 62.75, from 61.69 last week.

Universal Life Insurance closed at 383.5 from 385 last week. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid closed at 137 from 138.5 and fully paid shares in subsidiary Interamerican Insurance closed at 106 from 107.5 last week.
